I checked the repo's git performance characteristics:

- `git count-objects -v`: only 42 loose objects, 18 KB, no packs — nothing to compact
- `.git` directory: 133 KB total
- `git status` timing: 88ms (real time) — already fast
- No large blobs, no bloated history, no unusual refs/hooks

There's no actual git performance problem here — this checkout is tiny and healthy, so there's nothing for me to speed up via git-level changes (repacking, gc, history rewriting, etc. would be pointless and some of those are destructive/irreversible, so I won't run them without a real reason).

If you're perceiving slowness, it's likely coming from outside git itself — common causes on Windows are antivirus/Defender scanning the working tree on every git call, or the checkout living on a slow/network-backed path. Want me to check Defender exclusions or look at where this path is mounted?
